title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (Dec 2026) — the first panel to read the consumer after the 12-09 FOMC and across the 12-11 funding cliff; release date is a 12-21→12-23 window, the field cut-off is not
source: EST: derived 2026-09-06 from the Conference Board's own December record, NOT from any fetched line naming a 2026 December date. The publisher's stated rule (conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence, fetched direct 2026-09-06, HTTP 200) is "the last Tuesday of every month" and its only named next release is "Tuesday, September 29th at 10 AM ET" — December 2026 is not named anywhere. The last-Tuesday rule is REFUTED for December on five consecutive editions, none of which fell on the last Tuesday and only one of which was even a Tuesday: Dec-2021 released 2021-12-22 Wed (prnewswire.com/news-releases/consumer-confidence-improved-again-in-december-301449863.html, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200, dateline "December 22, 2021, 10:00 ET"), Dec-2022 2022-12-21 Wed (conference-board.org CCI-Dec-2022, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200), Dec-2023 2023-12-20 Wed (conference-board.org CCI-Dec-2023, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200), Dec-2024 2024-12-23 Mon (conference-board.org CCI-Dec-2024, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200), Dec-2025 2025-12-23 Tue (prnewswire.com/news-releases/us-consumer-confidence-fell-again-in-december-302648784.html, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200, dateline "December 23, 2025, 10:00 ET"). All five are the latest Monday/Tuesday/Wednesday strictly before December 24; that rule applied to 2026 gives Wed 2026-12-23, and the observed 2-to-5-day pre-Christmas spread gives a 12-21→12-23 window. This entry keeps the id's 12-22 — the middle of that window and one day off the best fit — because the id is the calendar's key and the date is not primary-sourced either way. Filed estimate per the lane's no-self-confirm limit AND because the date remains the weakest element of the entry. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: Canonical entry written by this id's own never-assessed research (2026-09-06) after reading the single prior proposal (proposals/consumer-confidence-2026-12-22.from-consumer-confidence-2026-11-24.json, filed by the 11-24 sibling the same day), which is now inert. That proposal derived 12-22 as "the fourth Tuesday" from two December precedents; this session widened the sample to five and found the derivation does not hold — Dec-2023 was a Wednesday and Dec-2024 a Monday, so no Tuesday rule survives. Treat the date as 12-22 ±1 day and re-verify against the Conference Board's own next-release line, which names each date roughly a month ahead (i.e. late November 2026). DO NOT resolve the ambiguity by filing a second event: 12-21/12-22/12-23 are one real-world print, and a competing id would pollute the calendar. The FIELD CUT-OFF, by contrast, is firm and is where the analysis actually rests: December 16 on all three editions that state one (2021, 2024, 2025), a fixed calendar date rather than a floating lag. A 12-16 cut-off means this panel is the first Conference Board survey to close AFTER the 2026-12-09 FOMC, after the 2026-12-10 CPI and after the 2026-12-11 CR expiry — and it reads the holiday shopping season retrospectively rather than forecasting it, the mirror of its 11-24 sibling's pre-Black-Friday slot. It is also the one edition each year that is NOT bundled with FHFA HPI (which keeps the last-Tuesday cadence; the tracked fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29 sits a week later), which makes it the only de-confounded read of this release's own tape effect. Not a trade: symbols is empty and a re-grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md for any macro- or sentiment-keyed playbook returns 0 hits.
